=========== entire checkpoint search ===========
entire checkpoint search — Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using semantic and keyword matching
Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using hybrid search (semantic + keyword),
powered by the Entire search service.

Requires authentication via 'entire login' (GitHub device flow).

By default, results are scoped to the current repository. Use --all-repos to
search across all accessible repos.

Run without arguments to open an interactive search. Results are
displayed in an interactive table. Use --json for machine-readable output.

CLI queries also support inline filters like author:<name>, date:<week|month>,
branch:<name>, repo:<owner/name>, and repo:* to search all accessible repos.

Current repo: et/devex/devdesk  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
      --all-repos        Search all accessible repos instead of just the current one
      --author string    Filter by author name
      --branch string    Filter by branch name
      --case-sensitive   Case-sensitive code search (only with --code)
      --code             Search code content across repositories
      --date string      Filter by time period (week or month)
      --json             Output as JSON
      --limit int        Maximum number of results (per page for checkpoint search, total for --code) (default 10)
      --page int         Page number (1-based) (default 1)
      --repo string      Filter by repository (gh/owner/repo, et/proj/repo, owner/repo, ULID, or *)
=========== entire checkpoint explain ===========
entire checkpoint explain — Explain a session, commit, or checkpoint
Explain provides human-readable context about sessions, commits, and checkpoints.

Use this command to understand what happened during agent-driven development,
either for self-review or to understand a teammate's work.

By default, shows checkpoints on the current branch. Pass a checkpoint ID or
commit SHA as a positional argument to explain a specific item, or use flags.

Viewing specific items:
  entire explain <id-or-sha>           Auto-detects checkpoint ID or commit SHA
  entire explain --checkpoint <id>     Force interpretation as checkpoint ID
  entire explain --commit <ref>        Force interpretation as commit ref

Filtering the list view:
  --session      Filter checkpoints by session ID (or prefix)

Output verbosity levels (when explaining a specific item):
  Default:         Detailed view with scoped prompts (ID, session, tokens, intent, prompts, files)
  --short          Summary only (ID, session, timestamp, tokens, intent)
  --full           Parsed full transcript (all prompts/responses from entire session)
  --raw-transcript Raw transcript file (JSONL format)

Machine-readable export modes (additive surface for external consumers):
  --json           Metadata-only JSON. Lists checkpoints when no target is given;
                   emits a single checkpoint envelope when a target is supplied.
                   Transcript bytes are NEVER embedded in the JSON envelope.
  --transcript     Stream stored checkpoint transcript bytes (JSONL) to stdout
                   for the selected session. Same bytes as --raw-transcript
                   while checkpoints v1 is the checkpoint store.
  --session-index  Pick a session within a multi-session checkpoint (0-based).
                   Defaults to the latest session. Only meaningful with
                   --transcript or --raw-transcript.
  --limit          Cap the number of checkpoints returned by the list view.
                   Defaults to 100. When the cap is hit, a stderr note
                   says how many were skipped. Only meaningful with --json.

Summary generation:
  --generate    Generate an AI summary for the checkpoint
  --force       Regenerate even if a summary already exists (requires --generate)
=========== entire checkpoint list ===========
entire checkpoint list — List checkpoints on the current branch
List checkpoints on the current branch.

Optionally filter by session ID with --session.

Current repo: et/devex/devdesk  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
      --no-pager         Disable pager output
      --session string   Filter checkpoints by session ID (or prefix)
=========== entire checkpoint tokens ===========
entire checkpoint tokens — Show token usage and optimization recommendations for a checkpoint
Show token usage and optimization recommendations for a checkpoint.

The report reads committed checkpoint metadata using the same checkpoint
resolution path as 'entire checkpoint explain'. Checkpoint IDs may be abbreviated
as long as the prefix is unambiguous; positional targets may also resolve from a
commit ref with an Entire-Checkpoint trailer, and missing metadata may be fetched
from the checkpoint remote.

Use --compare <checkpoint-id> to compare this checkpoint against a previous
checkpoint and qualify observed token reduction or increase.

Current repo: et/devex/devdesk  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
      --agent-brief      Output compact next-step guidance for agents
      --compare string   Compare against a baseline checkpoint ID
      --json             Output as JSON

=========== api ===========
entire api — Make an authenticated request to an Entire API and print the response
Make an authenticated HTTP request to an Entire API and print the JSON response.

The CLI attaches the right bearer token and dials the right host for the
chosen backend, so you don't have to plumb auth yourself:

  --to core   the control plane (default): orgs, repos, mirrors, clusters, /me
  --to cell   your home entire-api cell: /me/* activity, repo aggregates

Use --jurisdiction <slug> (e.g. us, eu) to reach a specific jurisdiction's
entire-api cell instead of your home one; it implies --to cell.

<path> is the full path on that host, e.g. /api/v1/clusters. These
placeholders are filled from the current repo's origin remote:
  {owner} {repo}   the GitHub owner / repo
  {repo_id}        the repo's Entire ULID (from its mirror) — cells key on this

The method is GET unless a field/body is given (then POST); override with -X.

Current repo: et/devex/devdesk  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
  -F, --field stringArray       add a typed parameter in key=value format; true/false/null/numbers are converted (repeatable)
  -H, --header stringArray      add a request header in key:value format (repeatable)
  -i, --include                 print the response status line and headers too
      --input string            file with the request body ("-" for stdin)
  -j, --jurisdiction string     target a specific jurisdiction's cell (e.g. us, eu) instead of your home cell; implies --to cell
  -X, --method string           HTTP method (default GET, or POST when a field/body is given)
  -f, --raw-field stringArray   add a string parameter in key=value format (repeatable)
      --to string               which backend to call: core or cell (default "core")
=========== clean ===========
entire clean — Clean up Entire session data
Clean up Entire session data for the current HEAD commit.

By default, cleans session state and shadow branches for the current HEAD:
  - Session state files (.git/entire-sessions/<session-id>.json)
  - Shadow branch (entire/<commit-hash>-<worktree-hash>)

Use --all to clean all Entire session data across the repository:
  - All session state files (.git/entire-sessions/)
  - All shadow branches
  - Temporary files (.entire/tmp/)

Use --session <id> to clean a specific session only.

Without --force, prompts for confirmation before deleting.
Use --dry-run to preview what would be deleted without prompting.

Current repo: et/devex/devdesk  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
  -a, --all              Clean all session data across the repository
  -d, --dry-run          Preview what would be deleted without deleting
  -f, --force            Skip confirmation prompt and override active session guard
      --session string   Clean a specific session by ID
=========== configure ===========
entire configure — Update Entire settings in the current repository
Update non-agent Entire settings in the current repository.

Manages telemetry, git-hook installation mode, strategy options, and summary
provider configuration. Agent installation is handled by 'entire agent'.

Examples:
  entire configure                                # Show this help
  entire configure --telemetry=false              # Opt out of telemetry
  entire configure --absolute-git-hook-path       # Reinstall git hook with absolute path
  entire configure --force                        # Reinstall git hook
  entire configure --checkpoint-remote github:org/checkpoints
  entire configure --checkpoint-backend refs      # Store each checkpoint as its own git ref
  entire configure --summarize-provider claude-code
  entire configure --summarize-timeout-seconds 300   # 5m deadline for explain --generate

Current repo: et/devex/devdesk  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
      --absolute-git-hook-path          Embed full binary path in git hooks (for GUI git clients that don't source shell profiles)
      --checkpoint-backend string       Checkpoint storage backend: branch (default) or refs (one git ref per checkpoint)
      --checkpoint-remote string        Checkpoint remote in provider:owner/repo format (e.g., github:org/checkpoints-repo)
  -f, --force                           Reinstall the Entire git hook
      --local                           Write settings to .entire/settings.local.json instead of .entire/settings.json
      --project                         Write settings to .entire/settings.json even if it already exists
      --skip-push-sessions              Disable automatic pushing of session logs on git push
      --summarize-model string          Set the model hint used by explain --generate
      --summarize-provider string       Set the provider used by explain --generate (e.g., claude-code, codex, gemini, pi, cursor, copilot-cli)
      --summarize-timeout-seconds int   Set the hard deadline (seconds) for explain --generate summary generation. 0 clears (falls back to 5m default).
      --telemetry                       Enable anonymous usage analytics (default true)
=========== enable ===========
entire enable — Enable Entire in current repository
Enable Entire with session tracking for your AI agent workflows.

If Entire is not yet configured, this runs the full configuration flow.
If Entire is already configured but disabled, this re-enables it.

If the current directory is not a git repository, Entire can initialize one
for you and (optionally) create a matching GitHub repository via the gh CLI.

Current repo: et/devex/devdesk  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
      --absolute-git-hook-path               Embed full binary path in git hooks (for GUI git clients that don't source shell profiles)
      --agent string                         Agent to set up hooks for (e.g., claude-code, codex, copilot-cli, cursor, factoryai-droid, gemini, opencode, pi; external agents on $PATH are also available). Enables non-interactive mode.
      --agent-help-skill entire agent-help   Install the stable Entire agent-help skill (points agents at entire agent-help) for selected agent(s)
      --checkpoint-backend string            Checkpoint storage backend: branch (default) or refs (one git ref per checkpoint)
      --checkpoint-remote string             Checkpoint remote in provider:owner/repo format (e.g., github:org/checkpoints-repo)
  -f, --force                                Force reinstall hooks (removes existing Entire hooks first)
      --init-repo                            If not a git repo, initialize one non-interactively
      --initial-commit-message string        Commit message for the initial commit when bootstrapping a new repo
      --local                                Write settings to .entire/settings.local.json instead of .entire/settings.json
      --no-github                            Initialize local git repo only; skip creating a GitHub remote
      --no-init-repo                         If not a git repo, exit instead of prompting to initialize one
      --project                              Write settings to .entire/settings.json even if it already exists
      --repo-name string                     GitHub repository name for the new repo (used when bootstrapping)
      --repo-owner string                    GitHub user or organization login for the new repo
      --repo-visibility string               GitHub repository visibility: public, private, or internal
      --search-skill                         Install the optional Entire search skill for selected agent(s)
      --skip-initial-commit                  Don't create the initial commit when bootstrapping a new repo
      --skip-push-sessions                   Disable automatic pushing of session logs on git push
      --telemetry                            Enable anonymous usage analytics (default true)
  -y, --yes                                  Accept all defaults without prompting (in a non-repo directory: init git, create private GitHub repo, commit; then enable all agents and accept telemetry)

content.content:
=========== review ===========
Run a multi-agent review against the current branch: several reviewer
agents review the change in parallel, then a single judge consolidates their
reports into the final verdict in a closing round. Reviews are saved as named
profiles in Entire settings and clone-local preferences. On first run, guided
setup writes a profile and asks before starting agents.

Flags:
  --configure    set up a review profile (shows available agents + profiles).
                 With --set-* flags it writes the profile non-interactively;
                 otherwise it opens the wizard (interactive) without starting agents.
  --set-agents   with --configure: comma-separated reviewer agents for the profile
  --set-judge    with --configure: the consolidating judge as agent[=model]
  --set-output   with --configure: where the verdict goes: local (default) or trail
  --local        with --configure: save to .entire/settings.local.json (just you)
                 instead of .entire/settings.json (shared). Interactive setup asks.
  --set-task     with --configure: the profile's canonical task text
  --set-model    with --configure: per-reviewer model as agent=model (repeatable)
  --set-slot     with --configure: a reviewer slot as agent[=model] (repeatable;
                 the same agent/model may repeat to run it multiple times)
  --edit         re-open the advanced profile skill picker
  --findings     browse local findings; pass a handle to print one saved run
  --agent NAME   run only one reviewer from the selected profile
  --list         list configured review profiles (their reviewers and judge)
  --agents       list the reviewer agents you can pass to --agent for the profile
  --model NAME   override the model for the --agent reviewer (requires --agent)
  --models       list the models each agent advertises (optionally --agent NAME)
  --profile NAME select a profile (also accepted as positional arg)
  --prompt TEXT  add one-off per-run instructions for this invocation
  --timeout DUR  optional hard cap on each reviewer before it's cancelled and
                 marked failed. No default — reviewers run until they finish,
                 like a directly-invoked skill. A positive value also bounds
                 the consolidating judge, which otherwise keeps its own 20m
=========== investigate ===========
Run a multi-agent investigation. Agents take turns appending findings,
evidence, and analysis to a shared findings document until quorum is reached.

Labs entry: investigate is experimental. We are actively refining it based on
user feedback.

Inputs (mutually exclusive):
  [seed-doc]              positional path to a starting findings file
  --issue-link <url>      GitHub issue or PR URL (resolved via gh)

When neither input is supplied and the spawn-time multi-agent picker fires,
the picker collects an "Investigation prompt" that becomes the topic for the
run.

Flags:
  --agents <csv>          override configured agents (comma-separated)
  --max-turns N           per-agent turn budget (default 2)
  --quorum N              approvals needed to terminate (0 = all agents)
  --continue <run-id>     resume an existing run
  --edit                  re-open the investigate config picker
  --findings              browse local investigation manifests
  --allow-untrusted-seed  required to run a non-interactive --issue-link
                          investigation (otherwise refused: the seed is
                          attacker-influenced GitHub content and agents run
                          with permission/sandbox bypass)

Subcommands:
  fix [run-id]            launch a coding agent with the run's findings as
                          grounded context
  show [run-id]           print a saved investigation's summary + findings
  clean [run-id|--all]    delete saved investigation artifacts

# Entire CLI

Entire records agent work as **checkpoints** — persistent records tied to commits — and tracks **sessions** across worktrees. This skill covers driving its CLI.

## Rule 1: the CLI documents itself — never guess flags

Entire ships a machine-readable help surface that always matches the installed binary:

```bash
entire agent-help                      # command map + when to use each
entire agent-help <command>            # exact flags for the installed version
entire agent-help <command> <sub>      # drill further
entire agent-help <command> --json     # structured output
```

**Read it before composing any non-trivial invocation.** The CLI evolves quickly; a
flag list memorised in a skill file goes stale, the self-help does not. This file
therefore documents *which command solves which problem* and the traps — command
names are stable, flags are not.

If a command errors on an unknown flag, do not guess a variant. Run
`entire agent-help <command>` and read the real surface.

## Rule 2: never ask the user for the repo

Entire auto-detects the repository from the git `origin` remote. You are already
inside it.

- Pass `--repo` **only** to target a *different* repo than the current one.
- Repo slugs take several forms: `gh/owner/repo` (GitHub-backed), `et/proj/repo`
  (Entire-native), plain `owner/repo`, or a ULID.

`entire agent-help` prints the detected repo in its footer — use that to confirm
which repo you are acting on before any write operation.

## Command map

| Need | Command |
|---|---|
| What did the agent do here? | `checkpoint explain`, `checkpoint list` |
| Find past work by meaning | `checkpoint search` |
| Who/what produced this line? | `why`, `blame` |
| Which agent knows this area? | `experts` |
| Session state, stop, resume | `session` |
| Activity summary | `recap`, `activity` |
| Written summary of recent work | `dispatch` |
| Is Entire on? | `status`, `enable`, `disable` |
| Something is stuck | `doctor` |
| Remove local session data | `clean` |
| Settings (telemetry, hooks, backend) | `configure` |
| Install agent hooks | `agent add/remove/list` |
| Raw API call | `api` |
| Orgs / projects / repos / access | `org`, `project`, `repo`, `grant` |
| Auth | `login`, `logout`, `auth` |
| Experimental workflows | `labs` |

## Provenance — the highest-value commands

These answer questions plain git cannot, because they join commits to the prompts
and sessions that produced them.

```bash
entire why <file>:42            # commit + checkpoint + prompt + session behind a line
entire blame <file>:12-20       # git-blame enriched with checkpoint metadata
entire blame <file> --long      # adds agent, model, author, session columns
entire experts <scope-or-query> # rank agent provenance for a code scope
entire experts --staged         # use staged paths as the scope
```

All three accept `--json`. Reach for `entire why` before speculating about *why*
code looks a certain way — it often returns the literal prompt that produced it.

## Search

```bash
entire checkpoint search "fix login"          # hybrid semantic + keyword, current repo
entire checkpoint search "..." --all-repos    # widen scope
entire checkpoint search "..." --code         # search code content instead
entire checkpoint search "..." --json --limit 20
```

Queries support inline filters: `author:<name>`, `date:<week|month>`,
`branch:<name>`, `repo:<owner/name>`, `repo:*`.

Requires `entire login` (GitHub device flow). Run with no arguments for an
interactive picker — **avoid that in an agent context**, pass a query and `--json`.

## Reading a checkpoint

```bash
entire checkpoint list                     # checkpoints on the current branch
entire checkpoint explain <id|sha>         # auto-detects checkpoint ID vs commit SHA
entire checkpoint explain <id> --short     # summary only
entire checkpoint explain <id> --json      # metadata only; never embeds transcript bytes
entire checkpoint explain <id> --transcript # stream raw JSONL transcript to stdout
```

Checkpoint IDs may be abbreviated to any unambiguous prefix. A commit carrying an
`Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer resolves as a positional target too.

`--json` and `--transcript` are deliberately separate surfaces: metadata never
carries transcript bytes. If you need both, make two calls.

## Sessions

```bash
entire session current            # active session for this worktree
entire session list               # across all worktrees
entire session info <id> --json
entire session stop               # interactive without an id
entire session resume <branch>
entire session adopt <id> --from ../other-worktree
```

## Token usage

```bash
entire checkpoint tokens <id>                      # usage + optimization advice
entire checkpoint tokens <id> --agent-brief         # compact next-step guidance for agents
entire checkpoint tokens <id> --compare <baseline>  # qualify a reduction
entire session tokens <id>
entire tokens profile                               # aggregate across checkpoints (labs)
```

`--agent-brief` is the right output mode when *you* are the consumer.

## Reporting

```bash
entire recap --week --view both     # day (default) | week | month | 90
entire recap --static               # non-interactive — required in agent context
entire activity                     # overview + recent sessions
entire activity --commits           # recent commits instead
entire dispatch --since 7d          # written summary of recent agent work
entire dispatch --local --all-branches
```

`recap` opens an interactive TUI by default. **Always pass `--static`** when you
are not a human at a terminal.

## Labs (experimental — surface may change)

```bash
entire review                       # multi-agent review of the branch, judge consolidates
entire review --list                # configured profiles
entire investigate <seed-doc>       # multi-agent investigation to quorum
entire investigate show <run-id>
entire import claude-code           # import Claude Code transcripts as read-only history
```

`entire review` is user-triggered and spawns real agents. Do not launch it on your
own initiative — surface it as a suggestion and let the user decide.

## Traps

**Interactive by default.** `recap`, `checkpoint search` with no query,
`session stop` with no id, `review --configure`, and `experts --tui` open TUIs
that will hang a non-interactive session. Pass `--static`, `--json`, or an explicit
argument. `ACCESSIBLE=1` in the environment swaps TUIs for plain-text prompts and
is a useful fallback.

**`entire clean` deletes work.** It removes session state and shadow branches.
Always `--dry-run` first; treat `--force --all` as destructive and confirm with the
user before running it.

**`entire investigate --issue-link` needs `--allow-untrusted-seed`** to run
non-interactively, because a GitHub issue is attacker-influenced content and the
agents run with permission bypass. That guard exists for a reason — do not add the
flag reflexively to silence the refusal.

**Pushes carry a second branch.** `git push` also pushes `entire/checkpoints/v1`.
A remote `HEAD` may resolve to that branch rather than `main`, which makes web UIs
appear to show "nothing" for the project. Check with `git ls-remote origin`.

**`entire api` is a real authenticated call.** `--to core` hits the control plane,
`--to cell` your home cell. Method defaults to GET, but becomes POST as soon as a
field or body is supplied — an accidental `-F` turns a read into a write. Path
placeholders `{owner}`, `{repo}`, `{repo_id}` are filled from the origin remote.

## Setup and repair

```bash
entire enable --agent claude-code   # non-interactive hook install
entire enable --agent-help-skill    # install Entire's own official agent-help skill
entire agent list                   # installed + available agents
entire status --detailed --json
entire doctor                       # diagnose stuck sessions, disconnected metadata branches
entire doctor --force               # auto-fix without prompting
entire configure --telemetry=false
```

`doctor` covers three known failure modes: metadata branches that share no common
ancestor with their remote, Codex hooks missing a trust hash, and sessions stuck in
ACTIVE (idle > 1h) or ENDED (uncondensed) phase.

Note that Entire ships an official `--agent-help-skill`. If a repo installs it,
prefer it as the authority for that repo and keep this skill for cross-repo habits.

flags with `entire agent-help <command>` rather than trusting this file.

content.text:
Confirmé : `--agent-help-skill` **est** booléen. L'affichage bizarre vient de la convention backtick de cobra — le \`entire agent-help\` de sa description a été extrait comme nom d'argument et retiré du texte. L'usage que j'ai documenté est correct.

La skill est créée et déjà enregistrée par le runtime :

**`~/.claude/skills/entire/SKILL.md`** — user-globale, donc active sur tous tes projets.

## Le choix de conception

Le CLI expose `entire agent-help`, décrit comme « machine-readable usage for coding agents (always matches the installed CLI) ». Autrement dit, Entire résout déjà le problème de la documentation qui dérive.

Écrire un catalogue de flags dans la skill aurait donc été activement nuisible : figé à la 0.8.42, il aurait contredit le binaire dès la version suivante, et un agent aurait fait confiance au fichier plutôt qu'à la source de vérité. La skill pose donc comme règle n°1 d'interroger `entire agent-help <command>` avant toute invocation non triviale, et se concentre sur ce qui ne bouge pas : **quelle commande résout quel problème**, et les pièges.

## Ce qu'elle contient

- **Règle 2 : ne jamais demander le repo.** Le CLI l'auto-détecte depuis `origin` et l'écrit lui-même en pied de chaque sortie ; `--repo` ne sert qu'à viser un *autre* repo.
- **Provenance** — `why`, `blame`, `experts`. Ce sont les commandes à vraie valeur ajoutée : elles relient une ligne de code au *prompt* qui l'a produite, ce que git seul ne peut pas faire.
- **Pièges**, la partie que le `--help` ne dit pas :
  - `recap`, `checkpoint search` sans requête, `session stop` sans id et `experts --tui` ouvrent des TUI qui **bloqueraient** une session non interactive → `--static` / `--json`, ou `ACCESSIBLE=1`.
  - `entire api` bascule GET → POST dès qu'on passe un `-F` : un flag de trop transforme une lecture en écriture.
  - `entire clean --force --all` détruit des données de session.
  - `investigate --allow-untrusted-seed` existe parce qu'une issue GitHub est du contenu influençable par un tiers alors que les agents tournent en bypass de permissions — à ne pas ajouter par réflexe pour faire taire le refus.
  - Le push embarque `entire/checkpoints/v1`, ce qui explique le `HEAD` distant de ton dépôt.

## Deux points à ta main

`entire review` lance de vrais agents en parallèle et c'est facturé — la skill demande explicitement de le proposer plutôt que de le déclencher seule.

Et Entire fournit sa **propre** skill officielle via `entire enable --agent-help-skill`. La mienne ne la remplace pas : si tu l'installes dans un repo, elle fait autorité localement, celle-ci gardant les habitudes transverses. Je l'ai signalé dans le fichier plutôt que de faire comme si elle n'existait pas.

Rien n'a été commité — cette skill vit dans `~/.claude/`, hors du dépôt.

---
name: entire-cli
description: Drive the Entire CLI (entire) for checkpoints, agent sessions, code provenance, and multi-agent review. Use when the user mentions Entire, checkpoints, session tracking, "entire why/blame/experts", agent activity recaps, or when a repo contains .entire/ and you need to inspect or manage tracked agent work.
origin: local-cli-analysis
tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob
---

# Entire CLI

Entire records agent work as **checkpoints** — persistent records tied to commits —
and tracks **sessions** across worktrees. This skill covers driving its CLI.

> Entire also ships its own managed skill named `entire`
> (`.claude/skills/entire/SKILL.md`, marked `ENTIRE-MANAGED`), installed by
> `entire enable --agent-help-skill`. That file is regenerated by the tooling —
> never hand-edit it. This skill is named `entire-cli` so the two coexist instead
> of shadowing each other: the managed one states the core rule, this one adds the
> workflows and traps.

## Rule 1: the CLI documents itself — never guess flags

Entire ships a machine-readable help surface that always matches the installed binary:

```bash
entire agent-help                      # command map + when to use each
entire agent-help <command>            # exact flags for the installed version
entire agent-help <command> <sub>      # drill further
entire agent-help <command> --json     # structured output
```

**Read it before composing any non-trivial invocation.** The CLI evolves quickly; a
flag list memorised in a skill file goes stale, the self-help does not. This file
therefore documents *which command solves which problem* and the traps — command
names are stable, flags are not.

If a command errors on an unknown flag, do not guess a variant. Run
`entire agent-help <command>` and read the real surface.

## Rule 2: never ask the user for the repo

Entire auto-detects the repository from the git `origin` remote. You are already
inside it.

- Pass `--repo` **only** to target a *different* repo than the current one.
- Repo slugs take several forms: `gh/owner/repo` (GitHub-backed), `et/proj/repo`
  (Entire-native), plain `owner/repo`, or a ULID.

`entire agent-help` prints the detected repo in its footer — use that to confirm
which repo you are acting on before any write operation.

## Command map

| Need | Command |
|---|---|
| What did the agent do here? | `checkpoint explain`, `checkpoint list` |
| Find past work by meaning | `checkpoint search` |
| Who/what produced this line? | `why`, `blame` |
| Which agent knows this area? | `experts` |
| Session state, stop, resume | `session` |
| Activity summary | `recap`, `activity` |
| Written summary of recent work | `dispatch` |
| Is Entire on? | `status`, `enable`, `disable` |
| Something is stuck | `doctor` |
| Remove local session data | `clean` |
| Settings (telemetry, hooks, backend) | `configure` |
| Install agent hooks | `agent add/remove/list` |
| Raw API call | `api` |
| Orgs / projects / repos / access | `org`, `project`, `repo`, `grant` |
| Auth | `login`, `logout`, `auth` |
| Experimental workflows | `labs` |

## Provenance — the highest-value commands

These answer questions plain git cannot, because they join commits to the prompts
and sessions that produced them.

```bash
entire why <file>:42            # commit + checkpoint + prompt + session behind a line
entire blame <file>:12-20       # git-blame enriched with checkpoint metadata
entire blame <file> --long      # adds agent, model, author, session columns
entire experts <scope-or-query> # rank agent provenance for a code scope
entire experts --staged         # use staged paths as the scope
```

All three accept `--json`. Reach for `entire why` before speculating about *why*
code looks a certain way — it often returns the literal prompt that produced it.

## Search

```bash
entire checkpoint search "fix login"          # hybrid semantic + keyword, current repo
entire checkpoint search "..." --all-repos    # widen scope
entire checkpoint search "..." --code         # search code content instead
entire checkpoint search "..." --json --limit 20
```

Queries support inline filters: `author:<name>`, `date:<week|month>`,
`branch:<name>`, `repo:<owner/name>`, `repo:*`.

Requires `entire login` (GitHub device flow). Run with no arguments for an
interactive picker — **avoid that in an agent context**, pass a query and `--json`.

## Reading a checkpoint

```bash
entire checkpoint list                      # checkpoints on the current branch
entire checkpoint explain <id|sha>          # auto-detects checkpoint ID vs commit SHA
entire checkpoint explain <id> --short      # summary only
entire checkpoint explain <id> --json       # metadata only; never embeds transcript bytes
entire checkpoint explain <id> --transcript # stream raw JSONL transcript to stdout
```

Checkpoint IDs may be abbreviated to any unambiguous prefix. A commit carrying an
`Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer resolves as a positional target too.

`--json` and `--transcript` are deliberately separate surfaces: metadata never
carries transcript bytes. If you need both, make two calls.

## Sessions

```bash
entire session current            # active session for this worktree
entire session list               # across all worktrees
entire session info <id> --json
entire session stop               # interactive without an id
entire session resume <branch>
entire session adopt <id> --from ../other-worktree
```

## Token usage

```bash
entire checkpoint tokens <id>                       # usage + optimization advice
entire checkpoint tokens <id> --agent-brief         # compact next-step guidance for agents
entire checkpoint tokens <id> --compare <baseline>  # qualify a reduction
entire session tokens <id>
entire tokens profile                               # aggregate across checkpoints (labs)
```

`--agent-brief` is the right output mode when *you* are the consumer.

## Reporting

```bash
entire recap --week --view both     # day (default) | week | month | 90
entire recap --static               # non-interactive — required in agent context
entire activity                     # overview + recent sessions
entire activity --commits           # recent commits instead
entire dispatch --since 7d          # written summary of recent agent work
entire dispatch --local --all-branches
```

`recap` opens an interactive TUI by default. **Always pass `--static`** when you
are not a human at a terminal.

## Labs (experimental — surface may change)

```bash
entire review                       # multi-agent review of the branch, judge consolidates
entire review --list                # configured profiles
entire investigate <seed-doc>       # multi-agent investigation to quorum
entire investigate show <run-id>
entire import claude-code           # import Claude Code transcripts as read-only history
```

`entire review` is user-triggered and spawns real agents. Do not launch it on your
own initiative — surface it as a suggestion and let the user decide.

## Traps

**Interactive by default.** `recap`, `checkpoint search` with no query,
`session stop` with no id, `review --configure`, and `experts --tui` open TUIs
that will hang a non-interactive session. Pass `--static`, `--json`, or an explicit
argument. `ACCESSIBLE=1` in the environment swaps TUIs for plain-text prompts and
is a useful fallback.

**`entire clean` deletes work.** It removes session state and shadow branches.
Always `--dry-run` first; treat `--force --all` as destructive and confirm with the
user before running it.

**`entire investigate --issue-link` needs `--allow-untrusted-seed`** to run
non-interactively, because a GitHub issue is attacker-influenced content and the
agents run with permission bypass. That guard exists for a reason — do not add the
flag reflexively to silence the refusal.

**Pushes carry a second branch.** `git push` also pushes `entire/checkpoints/v1`.
A remote `HEAD` may resolve to that branch rather than `main`, which makes web UIs
appear to show "nothing" for the project. Check with `git ls-remote origin`.

**`entire api` is a real authenticated call.** `--to core` hits the control plane,
`--to cell` your home cell. Method defaults to GET, but becomes POST as soon as a
field or body is supplied — an accidental `-F` turns a read into a write. Path
placeholders `{owner}`, `{repo}`, `{repo_id}` are filled from the origin remote.

## Setup and repair

```bash
entire enable --agent claude-code   # non-interactive hook install
entire enable --agent-help-skill    # install Entire's own managed skill (boolean flag)
entire agent list                   # installed + available agents
entire status --detailed --json
entire doctor                       # diagnose stuck sessions, disconnected metadata branches
entire doctor --force               # auto-fix without prompting
entire configure --telemetry=false
```

`doctor` covers three known failure modes: metadata branches that share no common
ancestor with their remote, Codex hooks missing a trust hash, and sessions stuck in
ACTIVE (idle > 1h) or ENDED (uncondensed) phase.

---

Authored against **Entire CLI 0.8.42**. Command names are the stable surface; verify
flags with `entire agent-help <command>` rather than trusting this file.

content.text:
Commité et poussé.

```
989decc chore: track the Entire-managed agent-help skill
```

**Vérification côté serveur** — les deux branches sont bien à jour :

```
989decc  refs/heads/main                    = local main
7ad2728  refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1   = local
```

Le premier `push` a affiché `fatal: ... HTTP 400: empty request body` alors que la donnée était déjà passée : `ls-remote` confirmait déjà `main` à `989decc`. Le second passage rend `Everything up-to-date` avec un code 0. C'était donc un artefact du wrapper git d'Entire — un second push redondant avec un pack vide — et non un échec réel. Je le signale parce que le message est trompeur si tu le recroises.

## État final

| Emplacement | Skill | Statut |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.claude/skills/entire/` | celle que j'ai écrite (~7 Ko) | intacte, globale, non versionnée |
| `devdesk/.claude/skills/entire/` | `ENTIRE-MANAGED` (652 o) | **commitée** |

J'ai supprimé le `entire-cli` que j'avais créé dans devdesk.

Une conséquence à connaître : les deux portent le nom `entire`, et les skills projet priment sur les skills user. Dans devdesk, c'est donc la version managée d'Entire qui s'applique, et la tienne est masquée. Dans tous tes autres dépôts, c'est la tienne qui joue. C'est cohérent avec ce que tu as demandé — je le mentionne pour que le comportement ne te surprenne pas.

Le message de commit précise que le fichier est généré et porte un marqueur `ENTIRE-MANAGED`, donc qu'il ne faut pas l'éditer à la main : il se rafraîchit en relançant `entire enable --agent-help-skill`, ce qui produira un diff quand le CLI changera sa formulation.

content.text:
# Plan Command

This command creates a comprehensive implementation plan before writing any code. It accepts either free-form requirements or a PRD markdown file.

Run inline by default. Do not call the Task tool or any subagent by default. This keeps `/plan` usable from plugin installs that ship commands without agent files.

## What This Command Does

1. **Restate Requirements** - Clarify what needs to be built
2. **Identify Risks** - Surface potential issues and blockers
3. **Create Step Plan** - Break down implementation into phases
4. **Wait for Confirmation** - MUST receive user approval before proceeding

## When to Use

Use `/plan` when:
- Starting a new feature
- Making significant architectural changes
- Working on complex refactoring
- Multiple files/components will be affected
- Requirements are unclear or ambiguous

## How It Works

The assistant will:

1. **Analyze the request** and restate requirements in clear terms
2. **Ground the plan** in relevant codebase patterns when the repo is available
3. **Break down into phases** with specific, actionable steps
4. **Identify dependencies** between components
5. **Assess risks** and potential blockers
6. **Estimate complexity** (High/Medium/Low)
7. **Present the plan** and WAIT for your explicit confirmation

## Input Modes

| Input | Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `path/to/name.prd.md` | PRD artifact mode | Read the PRD, pick the next pending delivery milestone or implementation phase, and write `.claude/plans/{name}.plan.md` |
| Any other markdown path | Reference mode | Read the file as context and produce an inline plan |
| Free-form text | Conversational mode | Produce an inline plan |
| Empty input | Clarification mode | Ask what should be planned |

In PRD artifact mode, create `.claude/plans/` if needed. If the PRD contains a `Delivery Milestones` table, update only the selected row from `pending` to `in-progress` and set its `Plan` cell to the generated plan path. If the PRD uses the legacy `.claude/PRPs/prds/` format with `Implementation Phases`, read it without migrating paths.

## Pattern Grounding

Before writing the plan, search the codebase for conventions the implementation should mirror. Capture the top example for each relevant category with file references:

| Category | What to capture |
|---|---|
| Naming | File, function, type, command, or script naming in the affected area |
| Error handling | How failures are raised, returned, logged, or handled gracefully |
| Logging | Levels, format, and what gets logged |
| Data access | Repository, service, query, or filesystem patterns |
| Tests | Test file location, framework, fixtures, and assertion style |

If no similar code exists, state that explicitly. Do not invent a pattern.

## PRD Artifact Output

When called with a `.prd.md` file, write the plan to `.claude/plans/{kebab-case-name}.plan.md` using this structure:

````markdown
# Plan: {Feature Name}

**Source PRD**: {path}
**Selected Milestone**: {milestone or phase name}
**Complexity**: {Small | Medium | Large}

## Summary
{2-3 sentences}

## Patterns to Mirror
| Category | Source | Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| Naming | `path:line` | {short description} |
| Errors | `path:line` | {short description} |
| Tests | `path:line` | {short description} |

## Files to Change
| File | Action | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | CREATE / UPDATE / DELETE | {reason} |

## Tasks
### Task 1: {name}
- **Action**: {what to do}
- **Mirror**: {pattern to follow}
- **Validate**: {command that proves correctness}

## Validation
```bash
{project-specific validation commands}
```

## Risks
| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|

## Acceptance
- [ ] All tasks complete
- [ ] Validation passes
- [ ] Patterns mirrored, not reinvented
````

After writing the artifact, report its path and WAIT for confirmation before writing code.

## Example Usage

```
User: /plan I need to add real-time notifications when markets resolve

Assistant:
# Implementation Plan: Real-Time Market Resolution Notifications

## Requirements Restatement
- Send notifications to users when markets they're watching resolve
- Support multiple notification channels (in-app, email, webhook)
- Ensure notifications are delivered reliably
- Include market outcome and user's position result

## Implementation Phases

### Phase 1: Database Schema
- Add notifications table with columns: id, user_id, market_id, type, status, created_at
- Add user_notification_preferences table for channel preferences
- Create indexes on user_id and market_id for performance

### Phase 2: Notification Service
- Create notification service in lib/notifications.ts
- Implement notification queue using BullMQ/Redis
- Add retry logic for failed deliveries
- Create notification templates

### Phase 3: Integration Points
- Hook into market resolution logic (when status changes to "resolved")
- Query all users with positions in market
- Enqueue notifications for each user

### Phase 4: Frontend Components
- Create NotificationBell component in header
- Add NotificationList modal
- Implement real-time updates via Supabase subscriptions
- Add notification preferences page

## Dependencies
- Redis (for queue)
- Email service (SendGrid/Resend)
- Supabase real-time subscriptions

## Risks
- HIGH: Email deliverability (SPF/DKIM required)
- MEDIUM: Performance with 1000+ users per market
- MEDIUM: Notification spam if markets resolve frequently
- LOW: Real-time subscription overhead

## Estimated Complexity: MEDIUM
- Backend: 4-6 hours
- Frontend: 3-4 hours
- Testing: 2-3 hours
- Total: 9-13 hours

**WAITING FOR CONFIRMATION**: Proceed with this plan? (yes/no/modify)
```

## Important Notes

**CRITICAL**: This command will **NOT** write any code until you explicitly confirm the plan with "yes" or "proceed" or similar affirmative response.

If you want changes, respond with:
- "modify: [your changes]"
- "different approach: [alternative]"
- "skip phase 2 and do phase 3 first"

## Integration with Other Commands

After planning:
- Use the `tdd-workflow` skill to implement with test-driven development
- Use `/build-fix` if build errors occur
- Use `/code-review` to review completed implementation
- Use `/pr` or `/prp-pr` to open a pull request

> **Need requirements first?** Use `/plan-prd` for a lean PRD at `.claude/prds/{name}.prd.md`.
>
> **Need the legacy PRP flow?** Use `/prp-plan` for deep PRP planning with `.claude/PRPs/` artifacts. Use `/prp-implement` to execute those plans with rigorous validation loops.

## Optional Planner Agent

ECC also provides a `planner` agent for manual installs that include agent files. Use it only when the local runtime already exposes that subagent and the user explicitly asks you to delegate planning.

If the `planner` subagent is unavailable, continue planning inline instead of surfacing an "Agent type 'planner' not found" error.

For manual installs, the source file lives at:
`agents/planner.md`

content.text:
Mesures terminées. Un fait structurant : **aucun test n'exerce actuellement un `Update()` Bubble Tea**, et il n'y a aucun usage d'`httptest`. Les phases qui touchent aux vues n'ont donc pas de pattern à imiter — c'est de l'infrastructure à créer.

---

# Plan : atteindre 80 % de couverture

## Reformulation

Générer des tests pour porter la couverture de **9,0 % à 80 %**, en priorisant les zones à plus fort impact.

## L'arithmétique d'abord

Profil de couverture fusionné (`-coverpkg=./...`) sur l'ensemble du module :

| | Statements |
|---|---|
| Total du module | **11 526** |
| Couverts aujourd'hui | **1 039** (9,0 %) |
| Requis pour 80 % | **9 221** |
| **À couvrir en plus** | **+8 182** |

C'est une multiplication par ~8 du volume couvert. Au ratio observé sur mes propres tests de ce dépôt (`topology_parsers_test.go` : 398 lignes pour ~180 statements), cela représente de l'ordre de **10 000 à 18 000 lignes de test** — une suite de taille comparable à l'application elle-même (~33 k LOC).

Je le pose d'emblée parce que ça change la nature de la demande : ce n'est pas une tâche, c'est un chantier.

## Où est l'impact

Le déficit est très concentré. Six packages portent **6 617 statements non couverts, soit 65 % de l'écart total** :

| Package | Stmts | Couv. | Non couverts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `internal/ui/oci_resources` | 2 660 | 0 % | **2 660** |
| `internal/ui/netdiag` | 1 128 | 15,9 % | 949 |
| `internal/ui/workspaces` | 827 | 0 % | 827 |
| `internal/ui/security` | 812 | 0 % | 812 |
| `internal/app` | 782 | 6,6 % | 730 |
| `internal/ui/gitlab/explorer` | 690 | 0 % | 690 |

À lui seul, `oci_resources` représente **23 % du code du module** et un tiers de l'écart. Les six plus gros fichiers sont `oci_resources/update.go` (918), `security/model.go` (812), `app/app.go` (647), `explorer/model.go` (561), `docker/client.go` (542), `workspaces/model.go` (516).

Conséquence directe : **on ne peut pas atteindre 80 % en évitant les vues.** Les packages `ui/*` sont le code. Toute stratégie qui les contourne plafonne autour de 20 %.

## Ce qui rend l'objectif atteignable

Deux constats favorables relevés dans le code :

1. **Les constructeurs sont purs.** `New(cfg *config.Config)` ne fait aucune I/O — les appels Docker/réseau partent de `Init()` sous forme de `Cmd`. On peut donc instancier n'importe quelle vue en test sans Docker.
2. **`Update()` est une fonction pure** `(Model, Msg) → (Model, Cmd)` (règle 110 du projet, qui interdit toute mutation dans un `Cmd`). C'est précisément la propriété qui rend une machine à états testable : on injecte des messages synthétiques et on assert sur l'état.

Le rendu est minoritaire : les fichiers `*view*.go` / `*render*.go` ne pèsent que **1 046 statements (9,1 %)**, borne basse puisque certains `View()` vivent dans `model.go`. On peut donc viser 80 % global sans écrire de tests de rendu exhaustifs.

## Patterns à imiter

| Catégorie | Source | Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| Table-driven | `internal/command/parser_test.go` | `tests := []struct{name, in, want}` + `t.Run(tt.name, ...)` |
| Fixtures | `internal/ui/netdiag/topology_parsers_test.go` | Sortie CLI verbatim, jamais simplifiée à la main |
| Système de fichiers | `internal/cache/cache_test.go:186` | `t.TempDir()` + `t.Setenv("HOME", tmpDir)` |
| Nommage | `internal/registrymgr/nexus_test.go` | Noms de sous-tests en phrase descriptive du comportement |

**Absent du dépôt** — à créer, pas à imiter :
- Aucun test ne pilote un `Update()` Bubble Tea (zéro occurrence de `tea.` dans les `*_test.go`).
- Aucun usage d'`httptest` — les clients HTTP (`internal/oci`, `internal/gitlab`) n'ont pas de harnais serveur.
- Aucune injection de `exec.Command` — `internal/docker/client.go` (542 stmts) appelle le CLI Docker en dur, non testable en l'état.

## Phases

### Phase 0 — Harnais (prérequis, aucun gain de couverture)
Créer `internal/ui/testutil/` : constructeur de `Model` en état connu, helper d'envoi de séquences de `tea.KeyMsg` / `tea.WindowSizeMsg`, exécution d'un `Cmd` et récupération du `Msg` produit, assertions sur l'état.

Sans ça, chaque phase suivante réinvente le même échafaudage. C'est le seul investissement qui conditionne tout le reste.

### Phase 1 — Feuilles pures (+~740 → **15 %**)
`ui/components` (496, formulaires et modales autonomes, sans config), `ui/help`, `ui/shortcut`, complément `ui/theme`, `internal/oci` (`extractTarGz` avec une archive en mémoire), `internal/credentials`, `internal/registrymgr`.

Le meilleur rapport effort/gain : aucune dépendance, aucun harnais.

### Phase 2 — Machines à états moyennes (+~1 240 → **26 %**)
`ui/status` + `ui/status/components`, `ui/containers`, `ui/dashboard`, `ui/gitlab/auth`.

Valide le harnais de la phase 0 sur des vues de taille raisonnable avant de l'engager sur les grosses.

### Phase 3 — Grosses vues (+~2 470 → **48 %**)
`ui/workspaces`, `ui/gitlab/explorer`, `ui/security`, complément `ui/netdiag`.

### Phase 4 — `oci_resources` (+~1 995 → **65 %**)
Le morceau isolé, à traiter seul.

### Phase 5 — Routeur et coutures I/O (+~1 360 → **77 %**)
`internal/app` (routage, changement de contexte), `internal/scan`, `internal/docker`. Ce dernier **exige un refactor** : extraire une couture d'exécution (interface ou variable `execCommand`) pour rendre `client.go` testable.

### Phase 6 — Complément jusqu'à 80 % (+~400)
Le dernier segment est le moins rentable : rendu `View()` et branches d'erreur résiduelles.

## Risques

| Risque | Probabilité | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tests de rendu fragiles (chaînes lipgloss + ANSI) | **Haute** | Suite instable, maintenance coûteuse | Assertions sur sous-chaînes sémantiques, jamais sur le rendu complet ; pas de golden files ANSI |
| Phase 5 impose un refactor de `docker/client.go` | **Certaine** | Change du code de production sous des tests inexistants | Écrire d'abord les tests des parsers purs, puis introduire la couture |
| `test-race` non exécutable ici | Certaine | Les Cmd concurrents restent non validés | Nécessite gcc/clang sur le PATH — hors de ma portée, à faire en CI |
| Couverture prise pour de la qualité | Moyenne | 80 % atteints avec des tests sans valeur | Cibler les transitions d'état et les branches d'erreur, pas les getters |
| 9 fichiers > 800 lignes (plafond du projet) | — | Tests écrits sur une structure vouée à changer | Trancher : découper d'abord, ou assumer de retoucher les tests ensuite |

Ce dernier point mérite une décision explicite : `oci_resources/update.go` (1 698 lignes) et `security/model.go` (1 985) violent déjà la règle de taille du projet. Écrire ~2 000 statements de tests dessus avant de les découper fige leur structure actuelle.

## Complexité : **Large**

Aucune estimation en heures : l'incertitude sur la vitesse d'écriture des tests `Update()` est trop grande tant que la phase 0 n'a pas tourné sur une vraie vue. La phase 2 donnera un ratio mesuré, qui permettra de projeter le reste.

## Une modification que je recommande

L'objectif « 80 % » tel que formulé inclut le rendu et les branches défensives. Les phases 0 à 4 amènent à **65 % en couvrant toute la logique métier et toutes les machines à états** — c'est-à-dire l'intégralité du code où des bugs se logent réellement. Les 15 points restants s'achètent surtout en tests de rendu, qui sont le maillon le plus fragile de la suite.

Si tu veux le chiffre littéral, le plan ci-dessus y va. Si l'intention est la fiabilité, je te suggère de viser **80 % hors `View()`/rendu**, exclusion déclarée explicitement — objectif plus exigeant sur le code qui compte, et plus honnête que 80 % global gonflé au rendu.

---

**EN ATTENTE DE CONFIRMATION** — je n'écris aucun test avant ton accord. Réponds :
- `go` — exécuter le plan tel quel (cible : 80 % global)
- `go, hors rendu` — appliquer la variante recommandée
- `modify: ...` — ajuster phases, ordre ou cibles

10	)
11	
12	// ConfirmModal est une boîte de dialogue de confirmation
13	type ConfirmModal struct {
14		title   string
15		message string
16		focused bool // true = Yes, false = No
17		width   int
18		height  int
19	}
20	
21	// NewConfirmModal crée une nouvelle modal de confirmation
22	func NewConfirmModal(title, message string) *ConfirmModal {
23		return &ConfirmModal{
24			title:   title,
25			message: message,
26			focused: false, // Default sur "No" pour éviter les suppressions accidentelles
27		}
28	}
29	
30	// ConfirmModalYesMsg est envoyé quand l'utilisateur confirme
31	type ConfirmModalYesMsg struct{}
32	
33	// ConfirmModalNoMsg est envoyé quand l'utilisateur annule
34	type ConfirmModalNoMsg struct{}
35	
36	// Update met à jour la modal
37	func (m *ConfirmModal) Update(msg tea.Msg) (*ConfirmModal, tea.Cmd) {
38		switch msg := msg.(type) {
39		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
40			m.width = msg.Width
41			m.height = msg.Height
42	
43		case tea.KeyMsg:
44			switch msg.String() {
45			case "left", "right":
46				// Toggle entre Yes et No (Rule 135 — Tab exclusivement pour les onglets)
47				m.focused = !m.focused
48				return m, nil
49	
50			case "enter", " ":
51				// Confirmer la sélection
52				if m.focused {
53					return m, func() tea.Msg {
54						return ConfirmModalYesMsg{}
55					}
56				} else {
57					return m, func() tea.Msg {
58						return ConfirmModalNoMsg{}
59					}
60				}
61	
62			case "y", "Y":
63				// Raccourci pour Yes
64				return m, func() tea.Msg {
65					return ConfirmModalYesMsg{}
66				}
67	
68			case "n", "N", "esc":
69				// Raccourci pour No
70				return m, func() tea.Msg {
71					return ConfirmModalNoMsg{}
72				}
73			}
74		}
75	
76		return m, nil
77	}
78	
79	// View affiche la modal
80	func (m *ConfirmModal) View() string {
81		var b strings.Builder
82	
83		// Titre
84		b.WriteString(theme.TitleStyle.Render(m.title))
85		b.WriteString("\n\n")
86	
87		// Message
88		b.WriteString(m.message)
89		b.WriteString("\n\n")
90	
91		// Boutons
92		yes := theme.RenderButton("Yes", m.focused, "danger")
93		no := theme.RenderButton("No", !m.focused, "primary")
94	
95		buttons := yes + theme.Bg("  ") + no
96		b.WriteString(buttons)
97		b.WriteString("\n\n")
98	
99		return lipgloss.NewStyle().
100			Background(theme.ColorBackground).
101			Foreground(theme.ColorText).
102			Border(lipgloss.NormalBorder()).
103			BorderForeground(theme.ColorError).
104			BorderBackground(theme.ColorBackground).
105			Padding(1, 2).
106			Render(b.String())
107	}

47		}
48	}
49	
50	// SetDisplayWidth sets the full terminal width used for background padding.
51	// Call this whenever a tea.WindowSizeMsg is received.
52	func (w *WrappedInput) SetDisplayWidth(width int) {
53		w.displayWidth = width
54	}
55	
56	// Focus gives keyboard focus to the input and returns the blink command.
57	func (w *WrappedInput) Focus() tea.Cmd {
58		w.focused = true
59		return w.input.Focus()
60	}
61	
62	// Blur removes keyboard focus from the input.
63	func (w *WrappedInput) Blur() {
64		w.focused = false
65		w.input.Blur()
66	}
67	
68	// Value returns the current text value.
69	func (w WrappedInput) Value() string {
70		return w.input.Value()
71	}
72	
73	// Update handles Bubble Tea messages and returns the updated model.
74	func (w WrappedInput) Update(msg tea.Msg) (WrappedInput, tea.Cmd) {
75		var cmd tea.Cmd
76		w.input, cmd = w.input.Update(msg)
77		return w, cmd
78	}
79	
80	// View renders the word-wrapped content block padded to displayWidth.
81	// Each line is prefixed with a 2-char indent. When focused, a block cursor
82	// is drawn at the current rune position.
83	func (w WrappedInput) View() string {
84		value := w.input.Value()
85		lines := wrapInputLines(value, w.wrapWidth)
86		cursorPos := w.input.Position()
87	
88		if len(lines) == 0 {
89			if w.focused {
90				cur := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorText).Foreground(theme.ColorBackground).Render(" ")
91				return theme.PadWithBg("  "+cur, w.displayWidth)
92			}
93			return theme.PadWithBg(theme.DimStyle.Render("  "+w.input.Placeholder), w.displayWidth)
94		}
95	
96		cursorStyle := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorText).Foreground(theme.ColorBackground)
97	
98		var b strings.Builder
99		for i, wl := range lines {
100			runes := []rune(wl.text)
101			lineEnd := wl.startIndex + len(runes)
102	
103			var displayLine string
104			if w.focused && cursorPos >= wl.startIndex && cursorPos <= lineEnd {
105				col := cursorPos - wl.startIndex
106				before := string(runes[:col])
107				var cur, after string
108				if col < len(runes) {
109					cur = cursorStyle.Render(string(runes[col]))
110					after = string(runes[col+1:])
111				} else {
112					cur = cursorStyle.Render(" ")
113				}
114				displayLine = "  " + before + cur + after
115			} else {
116				displayLine = "  " + wl.text
117			}
118	
119			b.WriteString(theme.PadWithBg(displayLine, w.displayWidth))
120			if i < len(lines)-1 {
121				b.WriteString("\n")
122			}
123		}
124		return b.String()
125	}
126	
127	// wrappedLine holds one visual line and its start offset in the original rune slice.
128	type wrappedLine struct {
129		text       string
130		startIndex int
131	}
132	
133	// wrapInputLines splits text into visual lines of at most wrapWidth runes,
134	// breaking at word boundaries where possible, falling back to a hard break.
135	func wrapInputLines(text string, wrapWidth int) []wrappedLine {
136		if text == "" {
137			return nil
138		}
139		runes := []rune(text)
140		var lines []wrappedLine
141		start := 0
142	
143		for start < len(runes) {
144			end := start + wrapWidth
145			if end >= len(runes) {
146				lines = append(lines, wrappedLine{string(runes[start:]), start})
147				break
148			}
149			// Walk back to the last space within the allowed width.
150			breakAt := end
151			for breakAt > start && runes[breakAt] != ' ' {
152				breakAt--
153			}
154			if breakAt == start {
155				breakAt = end // no space found: hard break at wrapWidth
156			}
157			lines = append(lines, wrappedLine{string(runes[start:breakAt]), start})
158			start = breakAt
159			if start < len(runes) && runes[start] == ' ' {
160				start++ // consume the breaking space
161			}
162		}
163		return lines
164	}

Phase 0 et le gros de la phase 1 livrés. État vérifié :

| | Avant | Après |
|---|---|---|
| **Global** | 9,0 % | **12,7 %** |
| `internal/ui/components` | 0 % | **79,8 %** |
| `internal/ui/testutil` | — | **100 %** (nouveau) |

`go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt`, `golangci-lint` (0 issue) et `go test ./...` : tout passe.

## Phase 0 — le harnais

`internal/ui/testutil/` : `Key`/`Keys`/`Type`/`Resize` pour fabriquer les messages, `Msgs`/`Msg`/`MsgOf[T]` pour drainer les commandes en aplatissant l'arbre `tea.Batch`.

Le point non négociable était que `Key("enter").String()` rende bien `"enter"` : sinon chaque test de `Update()` bâti dessus exercerait silencieusement la branche `default` au lieu de celle visée, en passant au vert. J'ai donc écrit un auto-test qui vérifie le aller-retour sur les 24 touches utilisées dans le projet, plutôt que de me fier à ma lecture de l'API v1.

`Msgs` est documenté comme interdit aux `Cmd` bloquants — `tea.Tick` d'un timer de footer (Rule 128) figerait la suite pendant 3 secondes.

## Défauts trouvés

**1. `ReportModal.View()` produit de l'UTF-8 invalide.** La troncature `item[len(item)-52:]` découpe des **octets**. Sur un chemin non-ASCII, la coupe tombe au milieu d'un codepoint.

Ma première fixture est passée au vert à tort : avec « é » (2 octets) le décalage 36 tombait pile sur une frontière. J'ai reconstruit le cas avec « € » (3 octets, 90 octets au total, coupe à 38 — non multiple de 3), et le bug se manifeste. Le test le prouve maintenant au lieu de le supposer.

**2. La case « immediate deletion » du variant permanent est décrite comme non modifiable — elle ne l'est pas.** `NewDeleteConfirmModalPermanent` la pré-coche, mais `space` la décoche toujours. Un projet déjà marqué pour suppression pourrait donc partir en suppression non permanente.

**3. `wrapInputLines` boucle à l'infini si `wrapWidth <= 0`** (et fait croître `lines` sans borne → OOM). Non atteignable aujourd'hui : tous les appelants passent 60/80/100 selon la Rule 133. Latent, mais réel.

**4. `DeleteConfirmModal` utilise `Tab` pour naviguer entre champs**, ce que la Rule 135 réserve aux onglets.

Je n'ai corrigé aucun des quatre : le mandat était d'écrire des tests, et changer ces comportements modifie le contrat d'UI. Les points 1 et 2 sont documentés par des tests qui `t.Skip()` avec une consigne explicite le jour où c'est corrigé.

## Reste à faire

Le chantier est loin d'être terminé — c'est cohérent avec l'estimation du plan (+8 182 statements au total).

- **Phase 1, fin** : `ui/help`, `ui/shortcut`, complément `ui/theme`, `internal/oci`, `credentials`, `gitlab` — ~450 statements
- **Phases 2 à 6** : ~7 000 statements, dont `oci_resources` seul à 2 660

Le ratio mesuré sur ce lot donne une base de projection fiable pour la suite, ce que le plan attendait de la phase 2.

Veux-tu que je commit ce lot avant d'enchaîner sur la fin de la phase 1 ?

cd "C:/Users/anthoni/projects/entire/anthnel/devex/devdesk" && git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
test: add a Bubble Tea test harness and cover the components package

Coverage groundwork: 9.0% -> 12.7% overall, internal/ui/components 0% -> 79.8%.

internal/ui/testutil (new, 100% covered)
----------------------------------------
No test in this repo drove a Bubble Tea Update() before, so there was no pattern
to follow — this package establishes one. It builds messages (Key/Keys/Type/
Resize) and drains commands (Msgs/Msg/MsgOf[T]), flattening the tea.Batch tree.
It never starts a tea.Program.

The harness works because the codebase already guarantees the two properties it
needs: constructors are pure (I/O is deferred to Init() as Cmds), and Update() is
a pure function since Rule 110 forbids mutating the model inside a Cmd.

Key() round-tripping through tea.KeyMsg.String() is asserted rather than assumed:
the views dispatch on that method, so a wrong key type would send every test
through the default branch while still reporting green. All 24 key names used in
the project are checked.

Msgs() is documented as unsafe for blocking commands — a Rule 128 footer timer
built on tea.Tick would stall the suite for its full duration.

components tests
----------------
ConfirmModal, DeleteConfirmModal, ReportModal, WrappedInput, FilterBar and
CreationForm: focus and navigation state machines, closed-set cycling (Rule 132),
message emission, and the render invariants that are cheap to assert.

Four defects found and documented, none fixed here — this change is test-only and
altering them changes the UI contract:

1. ReportModal.View() emits invalid UTF-8. It truncates with
   item[len(item)-52:], slicing bytes rather than runes, so a non-ASCII path is
   cut mid-codepoint. The test fixture is built so the cut is guaranteed to land
   inside a 3-byte rune; an earlier 2-byte fixture passed by accident because the
   offset happened to fall on a boundary.

2. NewDeleteConfirmModalPermanent documents its checkbox as non-modifiable, but
   space still unchecks it — a project already marked for deletion could be sent
   through a non-permanent delete.

3. wrapInputLines loops forever when wrapWidth <= 0, growing its line slice
   without bound. Not reachable today: every caller passes 60/80/100 per Rule 133.

4. DeleteConfirmModal uses Tab to move between fields, which Rule 135 reserves
   for tab switching.

Defects 1 and 2 are pinned by tests that t.Skip() with instructions once fixed,
so the caveat disappears with the bug instead of rotting.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

# Idées de Fonctionnalités (Brainstorming)

## 1. 🕸️ Gestion et Diagnostic Réseau Avancés
- [x] **Visualisation topologique :** Un écran montrant quels conteneurs communiquent sur quels réseaux Docker pré-existants.
- [x] **Ping/Curl inter-conteneurs :** Une interface permettant d'exécuter rapidement un test de connectivité (ex: "Depuis *Conteneur A*, fais une requête HTTP vers *Conteneur B* : port 8080") sans avoir à ouvrir un shell manuellement.
- [ ] **Gestionnaire de "Port Forwarding" :** Un tableau de bord interactif pour gérer les redirections de ports vers la machine hôte.

## 2. 🛡️ Remédiation Sécurité Interactive (DevSecOps)
- [ ] **Assistance à la mise à jour (Auto-Patch) :** Après le scan Trivy, proposer de générer automatiquement un patch ou un `Dockerfile` mis à jour changeant la version de l'image de base pour corriger les CVE critiques.
- [ ] **Scan au niveau du code (SAST local) :** Intégrer des outils de linting de sécurité (comme `gitleaks` pour les secrets ou des linters IaC) directement dans la vue "Workspace".

## 3. 📉 Analyseur de Build et de Cache OCI
- [ ] **Visualisation des calques (Layers) :** Analyser une image locale pour afficher la taille de chaque couche (à la manière de l'outil `dive`).
  - Implémentation intégrée via `google/go-containerregistry` (approche "daemonless" sans dépendance au démon Docker).
  - Interaction directe avec les registres OCI (pull des manifestes et configs sans télécharger l'image entière).
  - Lecture en streaming des calques en mémoire (format `tar`) pour recréer l'arborescence des fichiers système.
  - Calcul de l'espace gaspillé via la détection des fichiers whiteouts (`.wh.`).
- [ ] **Analyse de "Cache Miss" :** Indiquer pourquoi la mise en cache d'un build a échoué (ex: "Le fichier package.json a été modifié, invalidant le cache").

## 4. 🚀 "Injection" d'Environnement (Dev Containers Spontanés)
- [ ] **Injection de configuration :** Permettre d'injecter les dotfiles du développeur (configuration vim, zsh, alias) dynamiquement lors de l'ouverture d'un terminal dans un conteneur.
- [ ] **Montage de volume "à chaud" :** Ajouter la possibilité de monter le répertoire de travail actuel (`pwd`) dans un conteneur existant à la volée pour tester un script local sans avoir à rebuild l'image.

## 5. 📊 Tableau de bord des Ressources (Mini-htop intégré)
- [ ] **Graphiques TUI :** Une vue avec des graphiques en TUI (utilisant des caractères braille) représentant l'utilisation en temps réel du CPU, de la RAM et des I/O réseau pour tous les conteneurs du projet sélectionné.
- [ ] **Alertes visuelles :** Possibilité de définir des alertes visuelles (ex: saturation mémoire).

# DevDesk Backlog

**Last Updated:** 2026-08-01

Open work for DevDesk: known defects, technical debt, and planned features.
Replaces the former `todo.md` at the repository root. Items completed there
(network topology visualisation, inter-container ping/curl) have been dropped
rather than carried over.

---

## 1. Known defects

None of these are fixed. Each is reachable from the current code unless noted.

### D1 — `ReportModal.View()` emits invalid UTF-8

`internal/ui/components/report_modal.go:136-139`

Long entries are truncated with `item[len(item)-52:]`, which slices **bytes**, not
runes. When the resulting offset falls inside a multi-byte codepoint the rendered
output is no longer valid UTF-8 and the terminal shows replacement characters.

Reachable with any non-ASCII repository path. Pinned by
`TestReportModalViewTruncationSplitsMultibyteRunes`, which `t.Skip()`s with
instructions once the truncation becomes rune-aware.

**Fix:** truncate on `[]rune`, and measure width with `runewidth` rather than
`len()`.

### D2 — The "permanent delete" checkbox is documented as locked but is not

`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:35` and `:99-105`

`NewDeleteConfirmModalPermanent` pre-checks *Immediate deletion* and its doc
comment states the box is non-modifiable ("pré-cochée et non modifiable"). Nothing
enforces that: `space` and `enter` on the checkbox still toggle it.

A project already marked for deletion can therefore be sent through a
grace-period delete that the caller does not expect. Pinned by

## Contenu du backlog

**1. Cinq défauts connus**, avec référence `fichier:ligne` vérifiée une par une, impact et piste de correction. Deux d'entre eux (l'UTF-8 invalide de `ReportModal`, la case « permanent » censée être verrouillée) sont épinglés par des tests qui `t.Skip()` avec consigne : l'entrée du backlog et le bug disparaissent ensemble, au lieu que la doc pourrisse.

J'ai explicitement marqué **D3 comme non atteignable** depuis les appelants actuels (la boucle infinie de `wrapInputLines` demande `wrapWidth <= 0`, or tous passent 60/80/100). Sans ça, quelqu'un y perdrait du temps avant de traiter les défauts réellement déclenchables.

**2. Dette technique** : les phases de couverture avec leurs volumes mesurés et ce qui est déjà fait, les **8** fichiers au-dessus du plafond de 800 lignes, et le détecteur de race qui exige un toolchain C.

J'ai consigné l'interaction entre les deux : écrire des milliers de statements de tests contre `security/model.go` (1785 lignes) ou `oci_resources/update.go` (1556) avant de les découper fige leur structure actuelle. C'est un arbitrage à prendre en connaissance de cause, pas à subir.

**3. Les fonctionnalités restantes** de `todo.md`, avec les détails d'implémentation préservés — notamment l'approche `go-containerregistry` « daemonless » et la détection des whiteouts `.wh.` pour la visualisation des calques.

## Deux décisions à te signaler

**Écrit en anglais.** `todo.md` était en français, mais tout `docs/` (README, CODEMAPS) est en anglais et le backlog se lira à côté d'eux. Dis-moi si tu préfères le français, la bascule est triviale.

**Les deux entrées cochées ont été abandonnées, pas reportées** — visualisation topologique et ping/curl inter-conteneurs sont faites. Tu avais demandé « les points encore à faire ».

Mes chiffres de fichiers surdimensionnés diffèrent de ceux que je t'avais donnés en début de session : je les ai remesurés plutôt que de recopier des valeurs devenues obsolètes.

content.content:
# GitHub Repository Requirement and Repository Types

Based on the documentation provided, **GitHub is not mandatory** to use Entire, though the platform supports both native and mirrored repositories.

## Entire-Native Repositories

The documentation describes "Entire Repositories" as "Git repositories stored in EntireDB, Entire's distributed Git database." These appear to be repositories created directly within Entire's system, storing not just code but also "sessions, checkpoints, transcripts, and review history."

## Mirrored GitHub Repositories

Alternatively, teams can use repository mirrors—synced copies of existing GitHub repositories hosted on Entire's infrastructure. According to the content, "Teams can keep working in GitHub, while developers and coding agents can use the regional Entire mirror as a Git remote."

## Feature Availability

The documentation emphasizes that mirrors provide regional Git access, supporting "many concurrent agent reads without overloading a single Git host." Both repository types appear designed for agent-driven development workflows.

However, the provided content doesn't explicitly detail which specific features are exclusive to native repositories versus mirrors. To understand the complete feature breakdown, you'd need to consult the full documentation index referenced at the beginning of the page.

# Checkpoint Search Troubleshooting

Based on the documentation, checkpoint search may return nothing or fail for several reasons:

**Authentication Issues**
Running `entire login` is required, as "Search only returns repositories and history your account can access."

**Indexing Delays**
Confirm work is "committed and pushed, then give Entire a couple minutes to index it."

**Repository Scope**
By default, CLI search targets the current repository. If searching elsewhere, use `--repo OWNER/REPO` or `--all-repos` flags.

**Verification Steps**
Check that your repository is Entire-enabled with `entire status`. If using the search Skill with agents, confirm "the project has the Skills workflow installed and that the agent can run `entire search --json`."

**Query Specificity**
Broad queries fail more often. Add contextual details like file names, error messages, feature names, or filters (branch, date, author) to improve results.

The documentation doesn't specify whether GitHub-backed repositories or mirrors are required prerequisites—only that authentication and proper indexing are necessary for search functionality.

A workaround is available—you can configure Git to fetch large files directly from GitHub while using the mirror for standard Git operations.

content.text:
## Réponse : non, GitHub n'est pas obligatoire

La doc est explicite. Les **Entire Repositories** sont un type de dépôt à part entière — « Git repositories stored in EntireDB, Entire's distributed Git database » — et sont documentés comme stockant « sessions, checkpoints, transcripts, and review history ». Le miroir GitHub est présenté comme l'*alternative* pour les équipes qui veulent rester sur GitHub, pas comme un prérequis.

Les prérequis de la recherche sémantique sont listés noir sur blanc, et **aucun ne mentionne GitHub** :

| Prérequis doc | Ton état |
|---|---|
| Authentifié via `entire login` | ✅ `@anthnel`, juridiction `us`, token en keychain |
| Checkpoints poussés | ✅ `refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1 = 2d0dbb6`, vérifié côté serveur |
| Délai d'indexation (« a couple minutes ») | ✅ le premier push date de 12:07, soit plus de 4 h |
| Requête spécifique | ✅ hors sujet — la commande échoue **avant** d'interroger quoi que ce soit |

La page « limitations » ne liste qu'une seule restriction connue, et elle ne concerne pas ça : Git LFS sur les miroirs.

## Donc c'est un écart entre la doc et le CLI

Trois erreurs concordantes, toutes déclenchées par le *forge* du remote et non par une absence de données :

```
entire checkpoint search "backlog"
  → parsing remote URL: remote is not a GitHub repository (host: aws-us-east-2.entire.io)

entire api --to cell "/api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/aggregates"
  → {repo_id} needs a GitHub repo; origin forge is "et"

entire api --to cell "/api/v1/me/activity?timezone=Europe/Paris"
  → { "repos": [], stats tous à zéro }
```

Le chemin client de recherche/activité exige une origine GitHub, ce qu'un dépôt `et/` ne peut structurellement pas fournir. Ce n'est donc pas une option de configuration que tu aurais manquée.

Ça explique aussi la capture : l'en-tête affiche `Checkpoint: 857b0958ac55 · 7ad2728` parce qu'il lit les **données git**, bien présentes ; le panneau *Activity* est vide parce qu'il lit la **couche d'analyse**, qui n'a rien ingéré.

## Ce que ça implique

Rien à corriger côté push — il est complet et vérifié. Trois voies :

1. **Le signaler à Entire.** Tu as un repro net : dépôt `et/` natif, tous les prérequis documentés satisfaits, trois messages d'erreur explicites. La doc promet une fonctionnalité que le CLI refuse.
2. **Tester le contournement** que tu m'as interrompu avant d'essayer : `--repo` accepte le format `et/proj/repo` d'après son aide, ce qui pourrait court-circuiter le parsing du remote. Non vérifié — je peux le lancer si tu veux.
3. **Passer par un miroir GitHub**, mais c'est un changement d'hébergement, pas un réglage.

Je note au passage que les skills `entire:*` que tu viens d'installer (`search`, `recall`, `replay`, `teach`) s'appuient toutes sur `entire search` — elles seront donc inopérantes sur ce dépôt tant que le point ci-dessus n'est pas levé.

**Sources :** [Repositories overview](https://docs.entire.io/guides/repositories/overview.md) · [Semantic search overview](https://docs.entire.io/guides/search/semantic-search/overview.md) · [Search troubleshooting](https://docs.entire.io/guides/search/semantic-search/troubleshooting.md) · [Repository limitations](https://docs.entire.io/guides/repositories/limitations.md)
